title: Entry-Level AI Jobs for College Students: Which Role to Apply For in 2026
summary: Entry-level AI jobs for college students: 8 roles, what they pay, and our analysis of 19,533 internship postings showing where AI hiring is growing.
body_markdown:
## TL;DR


• Entry-level AI jobs are growing but still rare. Only 4.2% of the 19,533 US internship postings we analyzed have an AI or machine learning term in the title, though that share rose from 3.1% in August to 6.0% in early November 2026.


• Jobs that require AI skills advertise 62% higher pay (PwC, 2026), but young workers in AI-exposed jobs are 19% behind their peers (Stanford, 2026).


• This guide covers 8 entry-level AI roles, who each one fits, what they pay and where they hire.


• About 36% of AI internships are research roles, many aimed at PhD students, so we show where undergrads actually get hired.


[Externships](https://www.extern.com/post/what-is-an-externship) are short, remote professional experience programs where you work on real projects for real companies, with guidance from people in the field. The[Wayfair n8n AI Agent Engineering Externship](https://www.extern.com/externships/wayfair-ai-agent-engineering-for-business-intelligence-nov-2026) and the[Pfizer AI Document Intelligence Externship](https://www.extern.com/externships/pfizer-advanced-ai-powered-document-intelligence-externship-nov-2026) give you real AI project work to show employers.[Explore all Externships](https://www.extern.com/externships) .

## What Counts as an Entry-Level AI Job in 2026?


An **entry-level AI job** is a role open to new grads or interns where building, training, deploying or managing AI systems is the core of the work. That's different from a regular job that happens to use AI tools. Both are growing, but they're not the same thing, and it changes what you should apply for.


The first group is still small. In 2025, about 2.5% of US job postings required AI skills, according to[Lightcast's analysis of the 2026 Stanford AI Index](https://lightcast.io/resources/blog/stanford-ai-2026) . On Handshake, more than 10% of active internships and 4.2% of full-time postings mentioned AI keywords as of March 2026, and the full-time share nearly doubled in a year ([Handshake, April 2026](https://joinhandshake.com/research/economic-research/class-of-2026-ai-outlook/) ).


And students got there first. Look at how fast AI use spread among graduating seniors, compared with how recently employers started asking for it.

So the gap isn't interest. It's proof. Handshake found 58% of seniors believe they need stronger AI skills to succeed at work, while only 28% say their program meaningfully integrated AI. And at Extern, artificial intelligence is one of the top three fields students tell us they want to explore next (18.7% in our 2026 post-program survey).


## Is AI Taking Entry-Level Jobs or Creating Them?


Both, depending on the kind of entry-level job. AI is shrinking routine starter work, while entry-level roles that demand judgment and AI fluency are growing. That's the single most important thing to understand before you apply.


The entry-level AI paradox


AI is shrinking routine starter jobs while growing entry-level roles that need judgment.


AI-exposed entry-level roles needing senior-style skills, change since 2019


+35%


Other entry-level roles, change since 2019


-10%


Employment gap for ages 22-25 in the most AI-exposed jobs vs. less-exposed peers


-19%


Advertised wage premium for jobs requiring AI skills


+62%


Sources:[PwC 2026 AI Jobs Barometer](https://pwc.com/gx/en/news-room/press-releases/2026/pwc-2026-ai-jobs-barometer.html) (US entry-level analysis, 2.4M jobs; wage premium);[Stanford Digital Economy Lab, Canaries in the Coal Mine](https://digitaleconomy.stanford.edu/publication/canaries-in-the-coal-mine/) (Aug 2026 update, ADP payroll data through June 2026).


• **The squeeze is real.** Employment for 22- to 25-year-olds in the most AI-exposed occupations is now 19% below where it would be if it had kept pace with less-exposed peers, according to the[August 2026 update](https://digitaleconomy.stanford.edu/publication/canaries-in-the-coal-mine/) of Stanford's "Canaries in the Coal Mine" study. Experienced workers show no comparable gap.


• **But a different kind of entry-level job is growing.** PwC's[2026 AI Jobs Barometer](https://pwc.com/gx/en/news-room/press-releases/2026/pwc-2026-ai-jobs-barometer.html) analyzed 2.4 million US entry-level jobs and found AI-exposed roles that require senior-style skills grew 35% since 2019, while other entry-level roles fell 10%.


• **Those roles pay more and ask more.** Jobs requiring AI skills advertised a 62% wage premium in PwC's data, and AI-exposed junior roles were seven times more likely to ask for skills like leadership and strategic thinking.


So the takeaway isn't "avoid AI" or "chase AI." It's this: apply for roles where you use AI to do judgment-heavy work, and skip the ones where AI does the whole job.


## What Did We Find in 19,533 Internship Postings?


We analyzed 19,533 US internship postings from 1,469 employers that Extern tracks, collected from company career sites and job boards between July 19 and November 6, 2026. We counted a posting as an AI internship when its title included an AI, machine learning or data science term. Here's what stood out.


### AI Internships Are Rising Fast


AI-titled internships made up 4.2% of all postings (823 of 19,533). But the share climbed quickly through the fall recruiting season, nearly doubling from August to early November.

Source: Extern analysis of 19,533 US internship postings from 1,469 employers, collected July 19 to November 6, 2026. AI = title contains an AI, machine learning or data science term. November covers six days.


And that timing matters. Many AI internships open later than finance or consulting roles, so if you stopped looking in September, you missed most of them.


### The PhD Wall


But not every AI internship is open to undergrads. The biggest single group is research roles, and many of them say "PhD" right in the title.

About 36% of the AI internships we found were research roles. Data science (19%) and ML or AI engineering (19%) were the main technical doors for bachelor's students. And 14% were non-technical: AI operations, automation, product, strategy and legal roles that business and humanities majors can target.


### Who's Hiring AI Interns


AI hiring isn't limited to tech companies. Of the 1,469 employers in our data, 240 (16%) posted at least one AI-titled internship, including automakers, defense contractors, drugmakers and banks.

We also found 52 internships with "agent," "LLM" or "generative AI" in the title, a category that barely existed two years ago. That matches the wider market: Lightcast found agentic AI skills went from 0.06% of postings in 2024 to 0.23% in 2025.


## Which Entry-Level AI Jobs Should You Apply For?


The right AI job depends on what you can show today. Here are 8 roles that hire students and new grads, from the most technical to the least.


### Machine Learning or AI Engineer


ML and AI engineers build and ship AI features: connecting models to products, building pipelines and making systems fast and reliable. Python, SQL, cloud basics and one shipped project are the usual bar.


BLS doesn't track ML engineers separately, but[software developers](https://www.bls.gov/ooh/computer-and-information-technology/software-developers.htm) earned a median of $135,980 in 2025, with 10% projected growth through 2035. Worried about automation? Our guide on[whether AI will replace software engineers](https://www.extern.com/post/will-ai-replace-software-engineers-guide) covers which parts of the job are changing.


### Data Scientist


Data scientists turn data into predictions and decisions, and it's the most common technical AI role open to bachelor's grads. Statistics, Python and the ability to explain results are what get you hired.


[Data scientists](https://www.bls.gov/ooh/math/data-scientists.htm) earned a median of $120,230 in 2025, and BLS projects 35% growth from 2025 to 2035, one of the fastest rates of any occupation. A bachelor's degree is the typical entry requirement. Here's our take on[whether AI will replace data scientists](https://www.extern.com/post/will-ai-replace-data-scientists-guide) .


### AI Research Assistant or Research Intern


Research roles push models forward: running experiments, reading papers and testing new methods. They're exciting, but they're also where the PhD wall is highest.


[Computer and information research scientists](https://www.bls.gov/ooh/computer-and-information-technology/computer-and-information-research-scientists.htm) earned a median of $140,300 in 2025, with 22% projected growth, but a master's degree is the typical entry requirement. Undergrads usually get in through a university lab or a program like the[Anthropic Fellows Program](https://www.extern.com/post/anthropic-fellows-program-guide) . Smaller research labs such as[Mistral AI](https://www.extern.com/post/mistral-ai-internship-guide) and[Sakana AI](https://www.extern.com/post/sakana-ai-internship-guide) also take research interns, and applied AI companies like[Tempus AI](https://www.extern.com/post/tempus-ai-internship-guide) in healthcare hire students who can work with real-world data.


### Forward Deployed or Solutions Engineer


Forward deployed engineers work directly with customers to make AI products actually work in their business. It's half engineering and half problem-solving with people, and AI companies are hiring for it fast.


If you like coding but don't want to sit behind a screen all day, read our[forward deployed engineer career guide](https://www.extern.com/post/forward-deployed-engineer-career-guide) for salaries and entry routes.


### AI Product Manager or Product Analyst


AI product people decide what an AI feature should do, who it's for and how to measure if it works. New grads usually start as associate product managers or product analysts.


You don't have to code, but you do need to understand what models can and can't do. Our guide on[whether AI will replace product managers](https://www.extern.com/post/will-ai-replace-product-managers-guide) explains how the role is shifting.


### AI Operations and Automation Analyst


This is the newest and most open lane. Automation analysts use AI agents and tools like n8n or Zapier to automate workflows across finance, marketing and operations teams.


It's also where agentic AI skills show up most. The[Wayfair n8n AI Agent Engineering Externship](https://www.extern.com/externships/wayfair-ai-agent-engineering-for-business-intelligence-nov-2026) has you build AI agents for business intelligence, which is exactly the kind of project these roles ask about.


### AI Trainer or Data Annotator


AI trainers review and rate model outputs, and annotators label data that models learn from. Most of these jobs are freelance or contract roles paid by the hour, and many don't require a degree.


But they're easy to start and hard to build a career on alone. Use them for income and exposure, then pair them with a project that shows you can do more than follow guidelines.


### AI Governance, Risk and Policy Analyst


Governance and risk analysts make sure AI is used safely and legally: checking for bias, privacy problems and compliance gaps. Law, policy, philosophy and business majors fit well here.


Document-heavy industries like pharma are early adopters. The[Pfizer AI Document Intelligence Externship](https://www.extern.com/externships/pfizer-advanced-ai-powered-document-intelligence-externship-nov-2026) puts you on that kind of real-world AI problem.


Not sure which lane fits? Start from your background.


Your background Best-fit entry-level AI roles Proof to build first

**PhD or research-track student** AI research intern, research assistant A paper, preprint or lab project


**Business or marketing** AI operations and automation analyst, AI product manager An automated workflow or AI agent that saves real time


**Law, policy or humanities** AI governance, risk and policy analyst; AI trainer A policy memo or model evaluation project


## How Much Do Entry-Level AI Jobs Pay?


AI-related roles are among the best-paid paths for new grads, with 2025 BLS medians between about $120,000 and $140,000 for the core technical occupations. Those are medians for all experience levels, though, so first-year pay is usually lower.

Medians cover all experience levels.


PwC's 62% wage premium is real, but read it carefully. It compares advertised pay in job postings that require AI skills with postings that don't, within the same sector. It doesn't mean learning one AI tool raises your own salary by 62%. And freelance AI training work is usually paid hourly, with rates that vary widely by project and expertise.


## How Do You Get an Entry-Level AI Job With No Experience?


You get your first AI job by picking one role, building one project that matches it and applying where AI hiring is actually happening. Here's the order that works best for the students we talk to.


1. **Pick one role.** Use the table above. Applying to "AI jobs" in general is the fastest way to get ignored.


2. **Learn the minimum stack for that role.** Python and SQL for technical roles; prompt design, workflow tools and data basics for operations and product roles. Our guide on[how to get into AI with no background](https://www.extern.com/post/how-to-get-into-ai-no-background-guide) maps out a starting path.


3. **Build one real project.** Recruiters want proof. See our[AI projects you can do with no experience](https://www.extern.com/post/ai-projects-no-experience) and[agentic AI project ideas](https://www.extern.com/post/agentic-ai-project-ideas-sprint-guide) , then put the result in a[portfolio](https://www.extern.com/post/student-portfolio-examples-guide) .


4. **Apply earlier and later than you think.** Our data shows AI internship postings kept rising into November, so keep checking after the September rush. Our[AI and ML internships guide](https://www.extern.com/post/ai-ml-internships-summer-2027-guide) tracks open programs.


5. **Look beyond AI labs.** Automakers, banks, drugmakers and consultancies hire AI interns too, often with fewer applicants per role.


6. **Show judgment, not just tools.** PwC's data says AI-exposed junior roles ask for senior skills, so in interviews explain why you made each decision, not just what you built.

## FAQ: Entry-Level AI Jobs


### What entry-level AI jobs can I get with no experience?


The most open entry points are AI operations and automation analyst, data annotator or AI trainer, and junior data analyst roles that use AI tools. Technical roles like data scientist need one or two strong projects. Start with a role that matches your skills today, then build experience toward the role you want.


### Do you need a computer science degree for AI jobs?


Not for every role. ML engineering and research usually want computer science, math or statistics, and research often wants a graduate degree. But AI product, operations, governance and training roles hire business, policy and humanities majors. About 14% of the AI internships we analyzed had non-technical titles.


### What is the highest paying entry-level AI job?


Research and engineering roles pay the most. BLS reports 2025 medians of $140,300 for computer and information research scientists and $135,980 for software developers, though research usually requires a master's. Data scientists earned $120,230 and are projected to grow 35% through 2035, the fastest of the three.


### Are there non-technical AI jobs for college students?


Yes. AI operations, automation, product, strategy, policy and governance roles all hire students without engineering backgrounds. In our analysis of 19,533 US internship postings, 14% of AI-titled internships were non-technical. Pair your major with AI tool skills and one project to stand out for these roles.


### Is AI a good career for college students in 2026?


Yes, if you target the right roles. Jobs requiring AI skills advertise 62% higher pay, according to PwC's 2026 barometer, and BLS projects 35% growth for data scientists. But routine entry-level work is shrinking, so focus on roles where you use AI for judgment-heavy work.


### Where can I find entry-level AI jobs and internships?


Check AI lab and big tech career sites, but don't stop there: automakers, banks, drugmakers and consulting firms post AI internships too. In our data, 240 of 1,469 employers posted at least one. Keep searching after September, because AI internship postings kept rising into November 2026.
